sentences.text: Polesinesuchus was an extinct stagonolepidid aetosaur, a group of armored reptiles, that lived during the Late Triassic period.
The single known specimen is estimated to be 76 centimeters long and likely represents a two-year-old juvenile.
This animal was originally distinguished from other aetosaurs by a unique combination of vertebral characters thought to be independent of growth stage.
Polesinesuchus aurelioi is the fifth aetosaur species discovered in South America.
The genus was named in 2014 by a team of seven researchers including Lúcio Roberto-da-Silva.
The only known fossil material of Polesinesuchus is a single partially articulated partial skeleton.
The holotype specimen, which is the specific specimen the species is based on, was collected from the Santa Maria Formation.
Anatomical study shows that Polesinesuchus lacks hyposphene articulations in its cervical and mid-dorsal vertebrae.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Polesinesuchus as the sister taxon of Aetobarbakinoides.
Close relatives of the Polesinesuchus clade include the South American genera Aetosauroides and Neoaetosauroides.
Fossil remains of Polesinesuchus, including skull and postcranial parts of a juvenile, were found in the Santa Maria Supersequence.
Polesinesuchus lived during the Carnian stage, approximately 237 to 227.3 million years ago, in southern Brazil.
In 2021, researchers found that many features distinguishing Polesinesuchus actually fall within the variation seen in juvenile Aetosauroides.
Due to similarities with juvenile Aetosauroides, Polesinesuchus has been suggested as a junior synonym of that genus.
